Rationale.Section: The owner framed the module on 2026-10-23 (translated from Russian): "what is taking shape is a built-in mini-git diff — a universal module, an object/function — which will show who changed what and when, and will help resolve edit conflicts." The agent-writes-a-document case is explicitly ONE target consumer, not the definition. The instruction was to brainstorm and record the requirement as its own module spec. Provenance: the brainstorm first shaped the "change batch" concept inside the agent-edits-visible backlog item (same day); the mini-git direction lifted that model out into a shared foundation, recorded as the top entry of the private product backlog. Scope decisions in this draft were taken by best judgment while the owner was away and are flagged in ApprovalBasis: (1) the dirty+liveReload repair fork, (2) session-scoped v1 without disk persistence.

Live-defect evidence from the same-day code read of src/renderer/src/store/editor.js APPLY_FILE_CHANGE (the function spans editor.js 2416-2573; cite the anchor, not the old line range): the reload branch gate is `if (autoSave || liveReload || readOnlyReload || tab.watchMode)` followed by `if (isSaved || liveReload || readOnlyReload || tab.watchMode)` — the second condition is true whenever liveReload is ON, regardless of isSaved. So with liveReload ON (the default, preferences.js:149) an external write to a dirty tab reads disk, records recordSnapshot(id, tab.markdown) (the only survival of the user's unsaved text: the five-deep ring feeding the manual diff view), and calls loadChange, silently replacing the buffer. The conflict banner path (BLOCK_RELOAD_CONFLICT) is reachable when liveReload is OFF and the reload gate declines, which includes the autoSave ON case with a dirty tab: the outer gate is true, the inner gate is false, and control falls through to BLOCK_RELOAD_CONFLICT. Consequence for this change: the repair (route dirty tabs at external write into the conflict banner instead of the silent swap) is small, urgent, and independent of the journal — hence the NonGoal recommendation to ship it as its own fix bundle rather than gating it on this module. If the owner folds it in at approval, the spec gains one Goal and the acceptance criteria gain a dirty-tab e2e case.

What the library generalizes, all verified 2026-10-23: (1) watcher — src-tauri/src/m013b/watch.rs, notify v7 + notify-debouncer-full, 200 ms debounce tick, `mt::watch::event` channel; renderer facade src/renderer/src/ipc/runtime/watch.ts; per-root subscriptions in store/project.js, per-open-file `_subscribeFileWatch` in store/editor.js. (2) live reload — liveReload default ON (preferences.js:149); loadChange preserves cursor/scrollTop/muyaIndexCursor, drops stale blocks (650a555f), scroll clamp `scrollToCordsAfterReload` (81213fe0); a 100 ms renderer settle and a per-path generation guard precede the disk read; hash-skip returns early when disk equals the buffer. (3) snapshots — store/diffSnapshots.js records pre-reload buffers into a five-deep ring at four recordSnapshot sites plus two recordOpenedSnapshot sites (BLOCK_SNAPSHOT_BEFORE_RELOAD_DATA / _DISK), consumed by components/editorWithTabs/diffView.vue. (4) diff engine — diff-match-patch ^1.0.5 (package.json:58) already powers that view. The journal is the generalization of (3) with attribution, in-app-edit triggers, a batch policy on top of (1)+(2), and a public diff API over (4).

The 200 ms Rust debounce coalesces rapid bursts but proves nothing about batch boundaries: a writer emitting events every ~150 ms never yields a quiet pause, so a quiet-gap-only policy would record one unbounded batch. Hence minimum quiet gap PLUS a forced cut under continuous writes, plus the atomic rename-write case (write-temp-then-rename agents) which arrives as a single discrete event and is the clean boundary. Exact numbers (gap, cut window) are plan-time from measurement; the policy's shape is the normative part.

Consumer map, all separate bundles: agent-edits-visible (flash, scrollbar rail, follow mode, ghost caret — reads journal batches and diffs); conflict merge UI (base/mine/theirs on journal states — also the proper long-term home for the dirty-tab repair); review/tracked-changes (accept/reject against journal states, while its review records stay INSIDE the document — the layer boundary both specs must restate: journal = local metadata, never in the file; review records = document content); file recovery (disk-backed states, v3). Cross-link: C-NOTIFICATION-SYSTEM R-5 already reserves the 'agent' source enum for future agent events; when agent-visibility lands, its notifications flow through that channel — the journal does not notify anyone.

Kind-level truth is all the file can prove: in-app = certainly this Mark; external = certainly external, identity unknown; system = certainly a Mark-applied transformation. The ladder above that (lsof process sampling = "probable", never fact; announced channel via the existing mark CLI = certain identity) is deliberately deferred with the model fields reserved, per the standing evidence-bounded-claims rule: consumer UI must never claim authorship the journal cannot prove.

Alternatives.Alternative: Real git (libgit2 bindings or shelling to git): rejected — footprint and complexity contradict the size-first positioning; branch/commit semantics are irrelevant to an editor buffer journal; a sandboxed MAS build cannot rely on external git.

Rust-side journal (SQLite in app-support, backend commands): deferred, not rejected — attractive when disk persistence arrives (v3); v1 stays renderer-side because every input (watcher events, buffers, content-derived block anchors (R-2 defines the tuple; muya ag-N ids are never used)) already lives there and no new IPC surface is justified yet.

Delta-only storage (git-like, store diffs not snapshots): deferred — markdown documents are small; full snapshots per record are simpler and self-verifying; deltas become an optimization if the performance gate or v3 retention demands them.

Grow store/diffSnapshots.js in place instead of a new module: rejected — the ring is a passive cache with one consumer; the journal needs attribution, in-app triggers, a batch policy and a public API, and burying those in a store file repeats the silo problem this change exists to remove.

Build the journal inside the agent-visibility feature bundle: rejected by the owner's own framing — the module is universal, with the agent case as consumer #1; coupling it to one feature's UI would re-fragment the foundation.

DeferredDecisions.Decision: The dirty+liveReload repair fork: separate small fix bundle (recommended, ships fast) vs folded into this change — owner decides at approval; ApprovalBasis carries the flag.

Disk persistence: storage format (JSON per document vs SQLite), location, caps and LRU numbers, plus the never-in-synced-folders rule's enforcement — the v3 change, with the backlog entry's storage/privacy paragraph as input.
Identity attribution channels (lsof heuristic, mark CLI announcement marker) and their confidence semantics.
History for closed files and non-open workspace files (watcher already covers roots; recording policy is a product decision).
Final library location and exact public API surface (candidate src/renderer/src/documentHistory/) — plan time.

Scenarios.Scenario: An agent rewrites a watched document in bursts while the owner has it open: each quiet pause closes a batch; the journal appends external records with timestamps; a future consumer asks diff(ring[-2], ring[-1]) and gets block-level hunks plus word detail — the data behind flash and rail, produced here, rendered elsewhere.

The owner types checklist ticks with autoSave OFF while an agent saves the file: today the buffer silently swaps (design-context evidence section); after the recommended separate repair the conflict banner asks; in both worlds the journal holds the pre-swap state and the exact external diff, and the future merge consumer turns them into base/mine/theirs.

A formatter rewrites the whole document from inside Mark: one system-trigger record; coarse diff collapses to a single whole-document hunk rather than thousands of line hunks — the >60% collapse rule already agreed for the rail consumer is data this API can express.
The tab is closed and reopened, or Mark relaunches: the session journal is gone — accepted v1 behavior; cross-session history is the v3 disk change, not a silent surprise.
